problem: Production readbacks for an earlier runtime-affecting merge stayed red after later non-runtime main commits advanced the live release marker.
root_cause: Production verification equated release-marker identity with exact triggering SHA and had no bounded Git-lineage rule for safe non-production descendant supersession.
fix: Accept exact SHA or a descendant whose entire diff is limited to explicit non-production paths; reject non-descendants and runtime-affecting descendants.
prevention: Use Git ancestry plus changed-path proof before accepting a newer live SHA.
Keep the non-production allowlist narrow and aligned with deployment paths-ignore.
Never accept runtime-affecting descendant supersession as equivalent production proof.
Apply the same rule to source snapshot, production release readback and canonical brand live readback.
